(Battle Ground, Washington) | college = [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (1996–2000) | draft_year = 2000 | career_start = 2001 | career_end = 2011 | career_position = [[Shooting guard]] | career_number = 24, 14 | team1 = [[Phoenix Eclipse]] | years1 = 2001–2002 | team2 = [[Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters]] | years2 = 2002 | team3 = [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka]] | years3 = 2002–2003 | team4 = [[Seattle SuperSonics]] | years4 = {{nbay|2003|full=y}} | team5 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years5 = {{nbay|2004|full=y}} | team6 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | years6 = {{nbay|2005|full=y}} | team7 = [[Houston Rockets]] | years7 = {{nbay|2005|end}} | team8 = [[Treviso Basket|Benetton Treviso]] | years8 = 2006 | team9 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years9 = {{nbay|2007|full=yes}} | team10 = [[Reno Bighorns]] | years10 = 2009 | team11 = [[Antalya Büyükşehir Belediyesi|Antalya BŞB]] | years11 = 2009–2010 | team12 = Reno Bighorns | years12 = 2010 | team13 = [[Aisin Seahorses]] | years13 = 2010–2011 | highlights = * 2× First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (1999, 2000) | bbr = frahmri01 }} '''Richard Anthony Frahm''' (born August 14, 1977) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He competed in the NCAA 3-point shootout his senior year, winning the men's division but was beaten by Jenny Cafferty of Rice. After he went undrafted following a college career at [[Gonzaga University]] and brief overseas stints, among others in the [[Philippine Basketball Association]], and in [[Turkey]], the {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|adj=on}} [[shooting guard]] signed with the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in 2003, where he played one season, averaging 3.4 points and one rebound per game. He was then made available in the 2004 [[expansion draft]], where he was selected by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]], but later waived. He was then signed by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2004-05 NBA season|2004–05 season]] for whom he averaged 3.8 points and 1.4 rebounds per game. Frahm joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the 2005–06 season. He scored 18 points on the season opener against Portland, his former team, but saw very limited action after. The Timberwolves waived him on March 16, 2006. The [[Houston Rockets]] claimed Frahm off waivers on March 20. After playing the 2006–07 season in [[Italy]] with [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]],{{Cite web |url=http://195.56.77.208/player/?id=FRA-RIC-77 |title=Richie Frahm, Benetton Treviso |access-date=October 27, 2007 |archive-date=February 10, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080210162445/http://195.56.77.208/player/?id=FRA-RIC-77 |url-status=dead }} he was signed by the [[Phoenix Suns]] for the [[2007-08 NBA season|2007–08 preseason]] but was waived on late October 2007 after playing two preseason games.[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/reporters_notebook.html Frahm Waived by Suns] Frahm was signed by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in December 2007.[http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/frahm_signed_071214.html Clippers Sign Guard Richie Frahm][https://web.archive.org/web/20071217171402/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=271214029 Kaman scores 23 points as Clippers edge reeling Grizz]. Posted December 14, 2007 He was waived on January 7, 2008.[http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/frahm_waived_080107.html?rss=true Clippers waive Frahm] Frahm played a total of 140 games in the NBA with career averages of 3.6 points, and 1.2 rebounds. His final NBA game was played on January 6, 2008, in an 82 - 88 loss to the San Antonio Spurs where he recorded 2 points and 1 rebound. Frahm was acquired by the [[NBADL|NBA D-League]] [[Reno Bighorns]] in February 2009.{{cite news | title= Bighorns add former Zags guard Richie Frahm to roster | date= February 19, 2009 | publisher= The Reno Gazette Journal | url= http://www.rgj.com/article/20090219/SPORTS10/90219027}} In 2010, Frahm signed with Japan's [[Aisin Seahorses]]. ==References== ==External links== *{{basketballstats|bbr=f/frahmri01|name=Richie Frahm}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Frahm, Richie}} [[Category:1977 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Italy]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Japan]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in the Philippines]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Turkey]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Antalya Büyükşehir Belediyesi players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Washington (state)]] [[Category:Charlotte Bobcats expansion draft picks]] [[Category:Darüşşafaka Basketbol players]] [[Category:Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball players]] [[Category:Houston Rockets players]] [[Category:Los Angeles Clippers players]] [[Category:Minnesota Timberwolves players]] [[Category:Pallacanestro Treviso players]] [[Category:People from Battle Ground, Washington]] [[Category:Philippine Basketball Association imports]] [[Category:Portland Trail Blazers players]] [[Category:Reno Bighorns players]] [[Category:SeaHorses Mikawa players]] [[Category:Seattle SuperSonics players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:TNT Tropang 5G players]]
